facts.statement: The type species of the genus Halisaurus is H. platyspondylus, which was named by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1869.
facts.quote: H. platyspondylus Marsh, 1869

facts.statement: Halisaurus is an extinct genus of mosasaur that was named by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1869.
facts.quote: Halisaurus is an extinct genus of mosasaur named by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1869.

facts.statement: Marsh renamed Halisaurus to Baptosaurus in 1870 because he thought the name was preoccupied by the fish Halosaurus.
facts.quote: It was renamed by Marsh to Baptosaurus in 1870, since he believed the name to already be preoccupied by the fish Halosaurus.

facts.statement: Under modern rules, the name Baptosaurus is considered a junior synonym of Halisaurus because the names differ by only one letter.
facts.quote: According to modern rules, a difference of a letter is enough and the substitute name is unneeded, making "Baptosaurus" a junior synonym.

facts.statement: More complete remains of Halisaurus have been found in North America and North Africa since its initial description.
facts.quote: Since its description, more complete remains have been uncovered from fossil deposits throughout the world with particularly complete remains found in North America and North Africa.

facts.statement: Halisaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous

facts.statement: Halisaurus appeared early in mosasaur evolution during the Santonian stage.
facts.quote: Halisaurus appeared relatively early in the evolutionary history of the mosasaurs, during the Santonian.

facts.statement: Halisaurus was a small mosasaur, reaching a length of 3 to 4 meters.
facts.quote: With a length of 3 - 4 m, Halisaurus was comparatively small by mosasaur standards.

facts.statement: Halisaurus had poorly differentiated flippers and lacked the hyperphalangy found in more advanced mosasaurs.
facts.quote: As in other halisaurines, the flippers of Halisaurus are poorly differentiated which means that the genus lacked the hyperphalangy of more advanced mosasaurs.

facts.statement: Despite its small size, Halisaurus was likely a relatively poor swimmer compared to other small mosasaurs.
facts.quote: That Halisaurus was a relatively poor swimmer is relatively surprising considering its small size, since other small and medium-sized mosasaurs were mostly adept swimmers.

facts.statement: In 2005, Nathalie Bardet and colleagues described the new species Halisaurus arambourgi and reassigned H. sternbergii to the genus Eonatator.
facts.quote: In 2005, the species Halisaurus sternbergii was reassigned to its own genus, Eonatator, along with the description of the new species Halisaurus arambourgi by Nathalie Bardet and colleagues.

facts.statement: A 2017 analysis by Tiago R. Simões and colleagues placed Halisaurus and the Halisaurinae as a sister group to the Mosasaurinae.
facts.quote: The most recent major phylogenetic analysis of mosasaurs, conducted by Tiago R. Simões and colleagues in May 2017, recovered Halisaurus and the rest of the Halisaurinae as a sister group to the Mosasaurinae.

facts.statement: At least four species of Halisaurus are currently considered valid: H. platyspondylus, H. arambourgi, H. hebae, and H. auriculatus.
facts.quote: At least four species of Halisaurus are considered valid: H. platyspondylus, H. arambourgi, H. hebae, and H. auriculatus.

facts.statement: The species H. onchognathus is considered dubious because all known remains were destroyed during the Second World War.
facts.quote: The species H. onchognathus, known from Campanian or Santonian deposits that were once part of the Western Interior Seaway, is considered dubious due to all the known remains of the species having been destroyed in the Second World War.

facts.statement: The type specimen of H. platyspondylus comes from the Maastrichtian-age New Egypt Formation in New Jersey.
facts.quote: Referred specimens include the type specimen YPM 444 (consisting of an angular and a basicranium fragment) from the New Egypt Formation (New Jersey), which is Maastrichtian in age.

facts.statement: H. platyspondylus ranged along the eastern coast of North America during the Middle to Late Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: The species is also known from the Mount Laurel and Merchantville Formations of Delaware, implying that the species ranged across the eastern coast of North America during the Middle to Late Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: H. arambourgi lived during the Late Maastrichtian and has been found in northern Africa and potentially the Middle East.
facts.quote: Like H. platyspondylus, H. arambourgi is Late Maastrichtian in age, though specimens of this species have been found across northern Africa and potentially in the Middle East.

facts.statement: The type specimen of H. arambourgi includes a disarticulated skull and 27 articulated vertebrae found near Khouribga in central Morocco.
facts.quote: The type specimen, MNHN PMC 14, is an incomplete skeleton that includes a disarticulated skull and 27 associated articulated vertebrae from the Grand Daoui area near Khouribga in central Morocco.

facts.statement: The pterygoid bone of H. arambourgi preserves twelve teeth, which is three more than found in H. platyspondylus.
facts.quote: Its pterygoid bone also preserves twelve teeth (three more than in H. platyspondylus).

facts.statement: In 2023, Shaker et al. named H. hebae based on fossils from the Late Cretaceous Dakhla Formation in Egypt.
facts.quote: In 2023, Shaker et al. named Halisaurus hebae, a new species of Halisaurus from the Late Cretaceous Dakhla Formation of Egypt, on the basis of disarticulated cranial elements, teeth, and vertebrae from the neck and back.

facts.statement: H. auriculatus was described in 2026 by Shaker et al. based on specimen NVP040 from the Dakhla Formation.
facts.quote: Halisaurus auriculatus, another species from the Dakhla Formation, was described in 2026 by Sharker et al. based on specimen NVP040, a partial disarticulated skull, several vertebrae, and part of a hindlimb.

facts.statement: The exact phylogenetic position of Halisaurus within the mosasaur family tree has long been controversial.
facts.quote: The exact position of Halisaurus within the larger mosasaur family tree has long been considered controversial.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that H. ("Phosphorosaurus") ponpetelegans might represent a distinct genus requiring a new name rather than belonging to Halisaurus.
facts.quote: They tentatively assigned these species to Halisaurus, with H. ("Phosphorosaurus") ponpetelegans possibly representing a distinct genus in need of a new name.

facts.statement: The genus Halisaurus was named by Marsh in 1869.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Marsh, 1869

facts.statement: Halisaurus belongs to the subfamily Halisaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Halisaurinae

facts.statement: Known species of Halisaurus include H. platyspondylus, H. ortlebi, H. arambourgi, and the uncertain H. onchognathus.

facts.statement: Halisaurus lived from the Santonian to the Danian, between 85.7 and 61.66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Danian (85.7 to 61.66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species for the genus Halisaurus is Halisaurus platyspondylus.

facts.quote: El programa sugirió que Halisaurus se ocultaba en las cuevas subacuáticas donde esperaba para atacar pequeños animales

rejected.quote: The holotype, consisting of an angular and a basicranium fragment discovered near Hornerstown, New Jersey, already revealed a relatively unique combination of features and prompted a new genus to be described.
